title: DGX Spark AI Cluster — Live Overview
description: One screen for the whole two-node cluster. Every vLLM number describes the distributed engine as a whole; every hardware number is per physical Spark. The engine state tile comes from a real completion (the engine controller), never from a process being alive; MONITORING_UNKNOWN means the telemetry is missing, not that the model is down.

panels.title: Cluster
panels.description: UP only when BOTH Sparks are reporting host metrics.

panels.title: Spark 1
panels.description: Head node — runs the API server and every service.

panels.title: Spark 2
panels.description: Worker node — runs the headless vLLM rank 1.

panels.title: vLLM engine
panels.description: THE engine state, from a real completion — not from a process being alive. cluster:vllm_service_state:code: the controller's state (readiness sequence: non-stream + stream completion, token progress, both GPUs, rank alive), overridden to QUEUEING while the primary is not READY/BUSY/DOWN and the orchestrator holds accepted requests durably queued for it (there is no fallback model: the same generation resumes when READY returns). DOWN stays DOWN with a queue. MONITORING_UNKNOWN means the telemetry is missing or the controller's verdict is stale (its snapshot stamp > 30 s old), never that the model is down — on 2026-09-11 'UP' here was a lie for five minutes; this tile cannot tell that lie.

panels.title: Readiness
panels.description: The v2 readiness sequence (CONTRACT §5), as the controller last proved it. 'proven' = the last canary completion succeeded (techsara_vllm_synthetic_success) AND both GPUs were seen working during the last readiness sequence (techsara_vllm_participation_ok). 'GPUs unproven' = the canary passes but the participation probe did not sample both GPU exporters above 30 % — on a TP=2 engine a finished completion already proves the all-reduce ran on both ranks, so this is a missing exporter sample, not a missing rank; the state tile will read DEGRADED. 'canary failing' = the last canary did not complete. 'unknown' = no canary has run since the controller started, or it is not scraped — absent is not zero.

panels.title: Queued requests
panels.description: Generations the orchestrator has accepted and durably queued for the main model (llm_queued_generations). Non-zero while the primary is not READY: each one is a person reading “Main model is recovering—your request is safely queued.” and the same generation resumes, exactly once, when READY returns. Orange past zero; VllmRequestsQueued fires after 2 minutes of it. 'none' when the orchestrator is not being scraped — absent is not zero.

panels.title: Worker rank
panels.description: Is the VLLM::Worker_TP1 process alive on Spark 2, per the worker sentinel? A TP=2 completion cannot finish without it. 'unknown' while the sentinel is unreachable — a 0 nobody can vouch for is not shown as ABSENT.

panels.title: Last successful inference
panels.description: Seconds since the controller's canary last completed a real streamed completion on the primary. The only liveness number here that a hung process cannot fake. Yellow past one minute (two canary intervals), red past five. 'no data' while the controller has seen no success since it started (STARTING), or is not being scraped.

panels.title: Canary TTFT
panels.description: Time to first token of the last SUCCESSFUL canary (2 tokens, no tools). ~0.4 s idle; the controller calls > 10 s DEGRADED. Shown only while the canary succeeds — a failed probe's timing is not a measurement.

panels.title: Running requests
panels.description: Whole distributed engine, not per node.

panels.title: Waiting requests
panels.description: Sustained non-zero means the scheduler is capacity-bound.

panels.title: Tokens/sec
panels.description: Generation tokens/sec across the cluster (1m rate).

panels.title: Incident duration
panels.description: How long the current incident has been open, from the controller's first detection. 'none' when there is no open incident (the series is absent by design, not zero).

panels.title: Recovery attempts (1h)
panels.description: Coordinated recoveries the controller STARTED in the last hour. The budget is 3 per hour; at 3 it stops restarting and goes DOWN with category budget_exhausted.

panels.title: Reason
panels.description: The controller's last failure category (CONTRACT §4, a bounded set — never free text). 'none' after a clean start or once VERIFY_STABILITY passes. Stays at the last category until the next incident, so read it with the state tile.

panels.title: GPU utilisation - per Spark
panels.description: Both GPUs should move together - they are one distributed model.

panels.title: GPU temperature - per Spark
panels.description: Amber at 86 C (the part's own slowdown point), red at 90 C (shutdown). The die is shared with the CPU complex, so heavy CPU load moves this too.

panels.title: GPU power - per Spark + combined
panels.description: Accelerator rail only - NOT whole-machine AC draw, which this hardware cannot measure at all.

panels.title: Unified memory - per Spark
panels.description: GB10 has no separate VRAM: model weights and KV cache live in host memory, so this IS the GPU memory figure.

panels.title: KV cache used
panels.description: One distributed engine, so this is cluster-wide by nature. Above ~90% vLLM starts preempting requests.

panels.title: Combined GPU power
panels.description: Spark 1 + Spark 2 accelerator power.

panels.title: Hottest GPU
panels.description: The hotter of the two Sparks.

panels.title: Avg GPU utilisation
panels.description: Averaged across both GPUs.

panels.title: Total GPU memory allocated
panels.description: Sum of CUDA context allocations on both Sparks. There is no capacity denominator on a unified-memory part.

panels.title: RoCE traffic
panels.description: NCCL tensor-parallel traffic between the Sparks.

panels.title: CPU utilisation - per Spark
panels.description: Host CPU, not the GPU. High CPU with idle GPUs usually means tokenisation, retrieval or the sync worker - not inference.

panels.title: Avg CPU utilisation
panels.description: Averaged across both Sparks.

panels.title: Ethernet traffic - per Spark
panels.description: Real LAN / internet throughput on the physical NICs. Virtual interfaces are excluded: counting veth and bridge alongside the NIC overstated spark-1 by 3.5x. This is NOT the RoCE fabric - RDMA bypasses these counters entirely.

panels.title: Combined ethernet
panels.description: Both Sparks together - the cluster's total traffic to the outside world.

panels.title: Data transferred
panels.description: Total bytes in + out over the dashboard's selected time range - change the range at the top right and this follows it.

panels.title: PostgreSQL
panels.description: Conversations, messages, web memory, research runs.

panels.title: DB connections
panels.description: Against PostgreSQL's default max_connections of 100.

panels.title: Biggest tables
panels.description: Live row estimates.

panels.title: Warehouse snapshot age
panels.description: How stale the Salesforce data is. A climbing age means answers come from an old copy while everything still looks healthy.

panels.title: Data on disk
panels.description: DuckDB + LanceDB + Parquet + reports combined.

panels.title: Live correlation — same time axis, so a tokens/sec dip can be explained
Engine state
panels.description: cluster:vllm_service_state:code over time, on the same axis as everything below it. A gap is a gap: nothing here draws a line across missing telemetry, and a stale controller verdict (snapshot stamp > 30 s old) is a gap too. QUEUEING is the primary not READY/BUSY/DOWN with requests held for it. With no series at all Grafana prints its own empty-result message for this panel type ('Data does not have a time field'); that is the same condition the tile above shows as MONITORING_UNKNOWN.

panels.title: Tokens/sec
panels.description: If this drops, read the next three panels left to right.

panels.title: GPU utilisation
panels.description: Both lines should move together — they are one distributed model.

panels.title: GPU temperature
panels.description: Correlate a tokens/sec dip here first — thermal throttling is visible.

panels.title: Unified memory used
panels.description: Memory pressure on a unified-memory machine.

panels.title: RoCE interconnect throughput - per Spark
panels.description: Traffic here while a prompt generates is the proof the two Sparks are exchanging tensors. Measured from the InfiniBand counters - RDMA is invisible to ordinary network counters.

panels.title: Database throughput
panels.description: PostgreSQL read throughput, 8 KiB blocks converted to bytes/sec. 'from disk' should stay near zero - anything else means the working set no longer fits in shared_buffers.

panels.title: KV cache utilisation
panels.description: A tokens/sec dip with this near 100% is capacity, not heat.

panels.title: CPU utilisation - per Spark
panels.description: On the same time axis as tokens/sec above, so a throughput dip that is CPU-bound rather than GPU-bound is visible.

panels.title: Ethernet throughput - per Spark
panels.description: TX and RX on the physical NICs of each Spark.

panels.title: Ethernet throughput - cluster total
panels.description: Both Sparks summed. Compare with RoCE throughput to the left: this is traffic leaving the cluster, that is traffic between the two nodes.

panels.title: Application endpoints
panels.description: Orchestrator, frontend and SearXNG expose no metrics; these are HTTP probes.

panels.title: Model services
panels.description: Router, embeddings, reranker and OCR (OCR runs on the worker when scripts/ocr.sh put it there).

panels.title: Data
panels.description: Full detail on the Databases / Data Stores dashboard.
